scoreProvenance: OpenScore Lieder releases its scores under CC0 (https://github.com/OpenScore/Lieder#license-and-acknowledgement). The MusicXML identification reads 'Transcribed by markpearse from IMSLP #522898' and carries rights 'OpenScore (CC0)'. Exact downloaded MXL bytes match the SHA-256 pinned in this config; no printed-edition imprint beyond that IMSLP reference is asserted.

Source part P1 is the Voice (one treble line with lyrics); P2 is Piano (two staves with explicitly numbered MusicXML voices 1/2 and 5/6). Each source voice is a separate MIDI track in one simultaneous compilation, not inferred from register. Two print-object="no" rests in piano bars 11 and 13 are omitted by the converter. Voice labels are encoding identities, not separated audio stems.

Nonstandard MusicXML other-dynamics texts ('a tempo', 'dolce marcato', 'poco rall.') are preserved as printed words via otherDynamicsWords, because LilyPond 2.24.4's converter would otherwise emit invalid identifiers; no note or rhythm changes.

Recording: Emma Eames, soprano, with piano, Victor 85057, 16 March 1905 (content/listen module; the Victor label gives the key as D-flat). The OpenScore source is in D-flat major and the transfer's tuning estimate is −1 cent, so no transposition is applied; the soprano line sounds as written.

Initial grace: the piano's opening D-flat2 acciaccatura (voice 5) gives every MIDI track one common 43/384-quarter lead, retained once in bar 1's quarter extent. The guarded grace-priming adapter places nonprinting grace skips before the opening triplet groups of the other voices so that the engraving does not duplicate the initial clef/key/time glyphs; the converted event arrays are identical with and without that priming (995 notes).

Inspection (MEAS, not aural): a per-note dominant-pitch ranking found the written vocal pitch ranked first among 64–89 in most sung notes, including the A-flat5 'right' hold (37.1–41 s), G-flat5/E-flat5/F5 'All's right with the' (41.8/42.6/44.9 s) and D-flat5 'world' from 46.5 s; misses are mostly short pickups under louder piano chords.

Initial-grace contexts synchronized by silent grace skips, retaining source notes and main-time durations: Original lc6212179.mxl P2 measure 1 direct note index 27 is the visible D-flat2 eighth acciaccatura in voice 5/staff 2, before the bass D-flat3 on the first beat. Synchronize the other voices with nonprinting, nonsounding grace skips after their original initial attributes (before the opening triplet group where a voice begins with one); retain every pitched grace and all main-time note/bar durations. This follows LilyPond's documented grace-skip remedy for key/time synchronization: https://lilypond.org/doc/v2.24/Documentation/notation/special-rhythmic-concerns#grace-notes .

endpointMeasurements.label: first
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS, cached Commons transfer (work/beach-years-at-the-spring-eames-1905-0-12.png, 36-56.png and pitch-band tables). The first score attack is the piano's D-flat2 grace (q0, voice 5). Its own band is at about −80 dB throughout the opening of this acoustic recording, below the horn's bass response, so it cannot be located directly. The following bar-1 chord (D-flat3 bass with A-flat3/F4/A-flat4; their D-flat4/D-flat5/A-flat5 partials) rises from about −36 to −16…−21 dB between 0.30 and 0.50 s, with the first librosa onset at 0.43 s. The first window therefore places the grace immediately before that rise, 43/384 quarter (about 0.05 s) ahead of the chord; this is a documented placement, not a measurement of the grace itself. At the end, the dominant-pitch trace shows the voice's held A-flat5 (“right”) at 37.5–41 s, G-flat5 at 41.75 s, E-flat5 at 42.5–43.5 s, F5 (“with the”) at 44.75–46 s and D-flat5 (“world”) from 46.5 s; piano onsets at 50.95/51.8/52.75 s are the bar-28 beat-2/beat-3 attacks and the final bar-29 chord. A first broad window (40–58 s) had selected the F5 entry near 45.0 s as the final chord; that candidate was rejected. Numerical and visual inspection only; no aural review is claimed.
